passes.focus: 事实证据、许可边界与操作限制
passes.notes: 本遍聚焦事实证据、许可与操作限制。范围声明把未入馆候选与40件基线隔离，年度评选/奖项/技术事实各有单独证据职责；不得将未发布年份或品牌声称升级为事实。Framework边界包括首代版本排除后代，DIY指南涵盖11/12代且2023修订不等于原始2021手册，维修材料不自动证明寿命、减排或图像授权。 维修证据限于操作指南指定代际/步骤与iFixit单次升级，说明兼容和操作风险不等于普遍可修或寿命数据。奖项原库Red Dot确认为Best of the Best而iF正文403；TIME当时价格/署名和tollbit复访限制留在记录，Ars样机性能只支持限定配置及用途场景，奖项/年度媒体/评测的证明范围不混淆。 readyExhibit对应来源细分五段支撑范围：TIME仅选品、iFixit仅单次升级、指南只限操作段，且相关性字段不把首发和后续板混成同一事实。媒体/设计评奖的“关注度”不证明实用效果；没有合法图像就用文字回退，素材可读与可转载是两回事。 Logitech来源校准细化操作条件：原版接收器/蓝牙、Flow需两机软件、USB-C仅充电且未承诺现OS支持；测试页的手型/右手取向和办公/游戏分栏不能变成普适人体工学结论。品牌汇总区将鼠标与包装奖拆开，Chicago与日本GOOD DESIGN分开，iF页面403，故正式使用限Red Dot。Fairphone候选2015欧洲版与2016外壳版本分开，奖项Pencil图示等级映射未核；设计参与者不充独立评论。 Ear (1)记录严格区分品牌产品页面与WIRED同期采访，且对当前售价/奖项/内部维修没有证据；OP-1原版适用范围和2011出货仅由周年回顾支持，不误作日级上市，field及其馆藏页面不充当original证据。Sound On Sound只作合成/录音工作流实例，Design S传闻不作奖项。Dyson具体版本、温度采样和展览奖年份继续与新款频率或单项编号缺口分开。 Dyson奖项仍限定2016获奖年与2017展览年，官方清单不等于单项数据库；资料没有首代说明书、独立测试、iF Gold或授权图。Roborock时间轴不证明各地销售，性能百分比不作独立测试；Popular Science年度选品和单机TechRadar评价不转换成大奖，Red Dot索引无法支持具体等级。 reMarkable 2的品牌宣传、硬件采访、Red Dot普通奖分别支撑不同范围；TIME入选只在品牌声明层，不能标成已读独立媒体年度条目。Xbox资料把上市与获奖年分开，IDEA主办方索引的奖类字段可见但正文403，外接开关体验仅个体博客且不代表各类残障需求。 Xbox外接开关源是单人自购经验，个人更新日期与原文章日期分列；D&AD Black Pencil仍是微软说法、IDEA索引非全文可读。Labo欧洲上市与澳洲日期分区域，当前OLED兼容提醒不倒灌成2018知识；TIME是系列年度选择，TIME review是Variety Kit单件体验，均不产生日本设计奖证据。 Nintendo年度来源披露了未核的赞助、佣金与署名，系列奖项范围与单套件体验严格分开。Zenfone的赢家证据仅为作者本人帖子镜像，原片段待核，不因为“compact”标题和ASUS规格就自动确认。LG商品SKU是美国版，Red Dot是2024普通奖且确认不重复计算同一产品在不同分类的列项；电池续航是附条件最大值，不意味着户外防护。 LG奖项来源只支撑2024普通Red Dot，SKU由美国官方商品页匹配，不将后续分类同物重复计数。aibo获2018金奖依官方展览清单；动态单项详情并未读，且设计访谈不支持情感疗效。Roomba博物馆记录的CC0限元数据、照片另有使用条件；来源不足以就绪或推定算法，不能将同一件藏品镜像列为第二独立源。 Roomba候选没有被抬成可入馆展项，来源量有限且证据只支持第一代大致时间/工作方式；相同机构镜像不独立。Ear (open)官方支持文档只说明挂耳调节/充电，不采纳健康风险绝无的表述；发布时间来自社区二手线索，Red Dot项目支持2025普通奖，iF字段不完整。该研究末尾仍标明整合未重读所有底层正文，候选未决项保留。pass2已连续完整覆盖。 Re-read [17500,21000): AMM01/02 identify official 2019 model and user-guide scope, The exhibit prose likewise says USB-C is charging, not wired data, and refuses image reuse absent rights/model verification. This is a real missing range restoration, not new evidence or an extra full pass.

passes.focus: 逐句文风候选及应保留的必要否定/历史原文理由
passes.notes: 本遍逐句观察文风并保留必要限制。开头用“年度科技媒体/博主选择与工业设计奖交叉研究”给出可读范围；选择规则紧跟证据分层，因此“奖项/销量/第一/知名度不自动入选”的否定是方法边界而非装饰性免责声明。Framework开篇的“日常使用承诺”用后续升级记录校验承诺，保留品牌自述和供件/操作限制。 字段编排连续把操作指南/实操、设计评奖、年度媒体、单件评测按各自用途展开；尤其保留独立来源也有工具销售倡议立场、TIME佣金与访问限制、Ars测试配置/游戏栏的否定性边界。这些不是冗余免责声明，而是防止把“可维修”“获奖”“性能”等词泛化。 exhibit文本保留“年度入选说明编辑关注”而非获奖效果；正文把某一次换板当个例，使用动作亦明确不是现场维修指令，受众可读且风险边界具体。字段中“可维修便携计算设备”明示为策展分类，不伪装来源事实。 MX Master 3的证据字段和原型号指南在语气上用短而可核对的动作词（连接、切换、滚动、充电），把“舒适”归评审意见、把人体健康风险排除。产品奖与品牌汇总、包装项目、无法读取的iF/Chicago字段按状态原样保留。 MX正文的文风用动作部位解释接口，同时明确不主张发明优先权；“便捷是否足以承担学习设置成本”的提问保留取舍而非宣传语。关联计算设备只作馆内阅读关系。Fairphone候选将社会设计和模块化主张同拆装不能解决软件支持/供应链责任的限制作对照；年份、版本与奖项图示映射未定，需保留待核。 Nothing Ear(1)档案以透明和AirPods识别问题开场，却明说外观不能证明维修性；它将2021采访和品牌页面、价格及后继型号严格切开，不把设计奖或年度选品补造出来。OP-1的创作界面描述带有四轨“隐喻”与使用取舍；保存2011年回顾的年份范围、original/field分界和设计奖传闻未知，避免把品牌叙事写成使用者共识。 Dyson选品字段保留“BEST 100”正式等级和缺少单项编号，避免作者把展览年份读成奖年。Roborock正文形成房间/地毯这一策展问题，但奖励等级缺失仍保留，不偷换TechRadar Choice或清洁百分比；来源联盟链接等披露保留在条目旁。 reMarkable语气通过“聚焦纸笔也限制颜色/通用应用”等并列取舍，保留产品理念而非价值判断；普通Red Dot与TIME原文未核查的否定留在证据结构中。Xbox段的兼容和使用范围按2018平台/外接开关分拆，个人适配体验不代替普适性结论。 Xbox段用简短事实和保留语区分“可配置”和“人人可直接使用”，特别保留平台兼容、外接开关、个体体验及非普遍代表性。Labo同样以纸板组装/屏幕反馈为具体场景，但地区日期、当前OLED兼容、套件层级各分开；年度系列获选与单一套装的历史体验不合并。 Labo年度入选的范围措辞重复刻意，保留“不是本套件独立奖项”这一必要否定。Zenfone条目采用条件式“部分核实”，直说原视频赢家尚待核；不靠论坛/镜像替代来源。LG书写问题把搬运整套箱体和场所转变具体化，但不把便携包装成无代价或防水能力。 LG确认奖项年份为2024而非候选产品2023年份；标题中的“beyond living room”转成具体携带整箱使用问题，不把电池上限写成保证续航。aibo文字留住作品与陪伴的表达，同时明确没有治疗效果、全球销售或动态奖项页字段证据；金奖来源是2018清单。 Roomba结尾以“不适合入选/证据单薄”保持编辑判断的低信心，镜像来源不再计独立证据；Ear (open)将2024日期留为二手线索、把iF字段留白，且不把评委音质/舒适赞语改写成测量结果。最后的整合限制说明原文没有声称全部重核；这条限制应连同候选缺口一并保留。pass3完整覆盖。

[80500,82613)：Samsung公告限于美国非Touch T7于2020-05-19可购及速度条件，不移植Touch/Shield；Logitech Japan公告把2015-11-05标为计划售日且旧摘录曾纠正，地区日期未证实实际发生。最终来源记录说明仅支持具体型号/版本，不能证明图片转载许可、当前在售、长期可靠性或全球影响。此段维持来源原有不同可信度、验证深度及许可否定。

passes.focus: 逐句文风候选及历史原文/必要否定的保留理由
passes.notes:
[0,3500)：头部“existing slugs are revisions”“original40 remains unchanged”“no new firsthand validation”三句作为批次身份边界应逐字保留，防止把编辑修订误写成新增展项或新实测。DX7首段从1983原代及型号排除写起，后接结构、用途、意义与限制，段落推进由演奏任务到参数操作再到外部连接；多次否定“自动录音”“后代格式”“后代结束日期”有必要，因为区分本机能力与策展推论。Yamaha设计者说明明确标为原厂视角，未伪装独立观察。文件字段如proposed-stable-check-live-before-import、无媒体权利假设和status待审需原样留作状态事实。
[3500,7000)：DX7元数据将正文状态、无图视频和权利未假定、冻结策展位置、无独立评价和停产日期未核等区分保留；这些否定是必要证据边界。接入Portastudio段落后，文风由声音概念切换为信号链条式解释，细分通道/轨道/监听，再叙录制—回听—叠录—合轨—混出。四轨不等于四独立输入的否定及合轨后灵活性减少的解释应保留；品牌目录刷新失败的说明不可删，因为说明来源与操作阅读的来源强度不同。
[7000,10500)：Portastudio的元数据把结构事实与段落来源绑定到CWC-S005/原厂历史；relatedSlugs、冻结chronicle位置只是策展关系，不意味着关联机型同一或媒体权限。HP正文用屏幕—纸页两端建立打印场景，文风从文件准备、耗材、版面到纸上阅读递进；保留“可替换不证明寿命/维护费用”这一必要否定，且不从历史照片臆造接口/驱动/按键。
[10500,14000)：LaserJet与EP-101比较按任务/对象而非优劣排列，保留印出文本/图形与计算器数字打印组件的不同。限制段中特意重复速度、盒页数的产品口径及不等同当代网络/彩色任务，避免由1984家族名扩展能力；品牌“安静/便利”只作为厂商措辞，须有实测才能升格。记录目前为候选原代条目、日期不代全球首发，非已授权媒体内容。
[14000,17500)：MessagePad段落层次为器物/系统命名、笔屏交互、检查与修正、意义比较及明确未知；将Newton解释成操作系统而非实体、将可识别与内容正确分开，均属防止时代错置的关键原句。原馆藏不支持具体菜单/同步/通信步骤，红外不代表任意无线同步。手持与舒适未作普遍判断，保留这种必要限定。
[17500,21000)：MessagePad结尾以relatedSlugs将Macintosh/PalmPilot作比较关联，不应把策展关系读成产品血缘；其冻结页面位置、无图像/视频及无权利假设属状态字段。Zip开头采用具体物件串联叙述（盘片—驱动器—文件），并强调可移除不等于无需适配；文本明确不凭照片臆测接口、不套后代容量兼容性、不用现代USB经验补热插拔/弹出步骤。这个反复的否定有助保留原代证据边界。
[21000,24500)：Zip限制段强调容量与实际文件数取决格式，可靠性/光盘竞争明确是CHM后期回顾，不扩大成每台故障或统一结束日。名词、日期、容量升级策略均按原代Zip 100填写；媒体/权利/状态字段区分图文准备和授权。文风用具体场景搭配校准性否定，保留“实物状态/资料完整性另查”的结尾，不把历史概述冒充对象检查。
[24500,28000)：Zip策展比较不是同一系统的同义改写，而是借带走盘片/设备分离解释迁移链条；标称容量不等同具体文件数。ScanSnap新段区分日本销售节点和后来的第四版操作手册，结构从纸路到程序缩略图，流程清楚但保留查页序/方向/内容的人工检查。OCR只限明信片功能，文件管理工作仍在人与软件，不能把一键启动写成自动可检索。
[28000,31500)：ScanSnap的媒体/chronicle状态仍为文字待导入、权利未假设；正文readerTakeaway用纸页到文件的方向与LaserJet对照，不混淆两设备。K380开始将全球公布与日本计划供货分别表达，主叙事围绕切换目标而非宣传“多设备”；标明原K380、排除2023 K380s，避免年代/型号污染。电池寿命有条件，配对数不等同并行输入。
[31500,35000)：K380关联设备及长来源ID清单只表示来源覆盖/策展对照，不等于一条条都是K380直接证据；正文状态和作者/产品版本关联需保留。媒体短评对象有姓名、日期、原K380和原网址，且商业联系未明。下一片段的shortcomings字符串虽刻意未补出负评、媒体优惠条件45欧元/无量化耐久测试，必须按历史原文原样保留；来源表不因篇幅长而删裁。
[38500,42000)：来源索引延续Apple初代设备公告、操作手册转录与技术规格，重点保留版本识别、证据深度和未核事项：Apple-1 PDF未做全册视觉校验，C64为电子转录非逐页扫描，IBM手册OCR未完成整册图像检查；初代iPad规格不混后代特性，Macintosh规格表异常字段不作推断。来源段的长串信息易被压成泛称，但原文的具体“未采用排名/销量/广告话语”是历史审核取舍，应照实保留。
[42000,45500)：来源文风大量以“已读哪些页、哪些未做视觉检查”这种方法句限定证据深度，须逐条保留具体页码与限制，不能压缩成笼统“核过”。iMac缩小模型记录不作项目实物来源，MacBook手册指定页而非其余型号。MessagePad博物馆对象条目范围是硬件与系统命名，未核销量/耐久/图像许可；阅读过的转录OCR错误也不等于可以跳过下载限制。
[45500,49000)：Newton时间线1993首发/1998产品线终止不能推出单机识别率或原代停售节点；Zip对象记录和时间线同属CHM，特意说明非独立，范围也没有故障/销量/许可。TR-808源记录开始进入厂商故事，含原Id与包名追溯。保存同机构与独立来源辨析，避免把登记数量叠加成证据权重。
[49000,52500)：TR-808来源序列把各条原始记录的ID、来源文件、support范围、机构及不独立性逐项留下。加拿大/英国Roland页面并非独立两源；TB-303的2019软件公告是回溯1981，需保留“回溯”的时间关系。厂商范围只支持指定型号功能，不能提升为可靠性/销量/图像许可证明。
[52500,56000)：TB-303条目收束后接DX7的Yamaha两条回顾资料，再到Tascam History；文字倾向短句明确机构、型号事实、方法和限制，措辞的具体角色对溯源重要。DX7两个厂方链接是同源集团，不能说独立互证；Tascam只支持1979原144身份。未来如压缩字段，不能删“不独立”“未核”等否定信息。
[56000,59500)：Tascam字段特别保留本轮刷新403和“沿用前次身份年份核查，操作由原目录支持”的出处差异，避免装作重新验证；PDF同样为厂商来源。EP-101的Epson记录是厂史，JSME虽独立条目但藏品展示于Epson馆，原文未核资料来源独立性。句子保留测量、销量、授权等未核边界，不把独立机构标签扩写成所有信息均独立。
[59500,63000)：JSME条目限定EP-101销售/结构并保留“实物展出在Epson馆”的来源独立性疑问；LaserJet两条HP/HPE历史属于同品牌分拆后资料，不可伪成外部评价。ScanSnap日本实际销售日期由PFU自家周年材料支持，故日期来源仍须标品牌身份；语言持续避免以厂商材料证明可靠性或当前状态。
[63000,66500)：Samsung来源仅用于Zip与后续T7的策展比较，公告限定美国、非Touch、2020-05-19及依主机的速度；K380资料为Logitech品牌公告与Logicool地区公告，不独立，计划售日不能作为实际销售。字段保存日期纠错记录，而不是淡化早期摘录错误。
[66500,70000)：Tom’s Hardware评测明确仅第1页、1TB、未看性能页/平台且含联盟链接；其观点不能超出评测样机/文章边界。Irish Times短评也仅支持署名作者/价格/原版和单人体验，未见明确缺点或量化条件，不替作者制造批评。来源结构保留原文对独立性、商业披露和未核项的谨慎语气。
[70000,73500)：Roland TB-303和Yamaha DX7条目明确将后代浏览器/Cloud能力排除，原厂身份与测量限制同列；Tascam目录原文保留原版型号、信号路线和商业资料性质。作者对文档段落与字段语体区别明显，字段句简洁而具体。
[73500,77000)：原目录操作深度限6页中的P1–3，不使用“首创/无损/耐用”宣传且不假定转载许可。HP来源只支持1984年3月原桌面机，拒绝静音和销量话术；MessagePad馆藏部分参数引用第三方，因此不是独立测量。史料说明中这些自我收窄限定应保留，避免将馆藏目录写成技术测试。
[70000,73500)：来源登记收尾Roland/Yamaha厂方回顾；特别排除后代浏览器/Cloud功能和独立音质体验，Tascam目录的操作范围只限文本所说几页。来源条目用型号、验证手段、授权和销量限制细分，不能以“官方源”概括抹掉这些范围。
[73500,77000)：Tascam原144的六页目录只重点读取P1–3并拒绝无损/耐久宣传；HP原桌面机来源是1984年3月厂史，非静音/销量证据且不套后代；MessagePad博物馆文本参数非独立实测；Zip博物馆时间线注明后续可靠性和竞争回顾不是单机故障结论。
[77000,80500)：Zip-100来源限制不采用容量升级、不推故障率/停售日；ScanSnap第四版手册只核107页中的前言及P24–54相关章节，非全册；K380厂家公告只是公布/供货计划。
[80500,82613)：T7仅美国非Touch型号公告，USB速度有条件，不移植Touch/Shield；K380日本来源明确纠正计划销售日与实际首售差异并限定日本版。最后仍保留不授转载许可、不证明当前可购/长期可靠性/全球影响。

passes.focus: 来源、日期、型号及其适用范围
passes.notes: 文件为Wikimedia Commons搜索响应的原始JSON。本段开头query是Denon AND 3000，但首条命中却是1698分数论文PDF扫描；该结果含Commons元数据类别与作者/扫描来源，当前不能据此认定与目标唱机有关。审读重点是保留原始查询条件和结果字段，避免把搜索命中当型号/媒体授权证据。 第一个离题命中显示PD类许可字段（Public domain、attribution false、Copyrighted False）来自Commons元数据，不足以建立本任务具体唱机照片授权。第二命中是Acta mathematica扫描卷，书目与数学主题明显无关；仅看到元数据字段，继续保持原始JSON读法，不跟随Credit中的外链。 第二条数学期刊的来源字段显示多伦多数学科学馆扫描/渥太华赞助、PD元数据；第三条Administrative Notes是美国政府印刷局扫描，亦与Denon设备无关。两个PDF均含公共领域许可字段，但它们是误命中，不可挪作设备素材许可；原文中链接只被阅读为字符串。 后续两个结果是1811年荷兰报纸和古代史微缩扫描书；报纸有具体出版者/发行日期等书目字段，古书有PD-old类别。它们都属于历史数字化材料而非Denon唱机照片，进一步说明Commons全文搜索结果可能由数字“3000”等低相关词触发，不能用许可元数据取代型号匹配。 古代史讲座微缩扫描资料由哥伦比亚大学图书馆贡献，元数据标PD；它同样不涉及目标型号。接着出现California Digital Library目录文档，还是馆藏/扫描记录而非音频设备。搜索结果的书目相关性失配，应作为文件用途/误命中观察而不是对结果图像作内容推测。 California Digital Library结果实际描述拿破仑纪念章目录，元数据归类为Public domain；随后乌菲齐古今绘画目录仍是错配的书籍扫描。元数据中“来源是Commons description page”仅说明该字段出处，不能当成权属链或型号归属；结果还反复包含Internet Archive/上传者信息，需区分扫描供给方与作品作者。 乌菲齐目录元数据称分册1890–1897，涉及绘画且PD-US expired；随后是美国印第安人词典扫描。检索内容离目标产品越发远，仍需要逐结果确认其标题、作者/主题和许可标签并避免复制/套用这些PD结论到DP-3000NE素材。 1903年美国人类学词典的出版时间、史密森尼作者字段及PD许可有明确来源，后面是关于版画/书籍收藏的法语目录；这些对象主题都与目标唱机无关。逐项标题/主题观察能证明搜索响应充斥历史书籍扫描，但本轮不对目标设备的Commons素材状态下结论。 另一结果是1667算术书，属于早期印刷书籍扫描；Commons关键词查询确有“3000”可能落在藏品目录数量/文献语境等非设备领域，需要继续通读看明示项目。此块许可类别依旧只适用于该文献本身，且微缩封面说明提醒数字扫描呈现方式与原件存在中介。 1667算术书采用公有领域标签；下一条是1915年荷兰画家作品目录，其作者是艺术史家，亦标PD-Art。元数据有时将公共领域归为版权状态，有时称使用条款；这些表述只绑定对应扫描文献，不是项目可发布照片许可。此搜索响应继续表现出数字书目误命中。 两个后续结果是1886和1895年Il Friuli地方报纸的不同期号，描述为政治/行政/文学/商业期刊，且均标公共领域/历史扫描。注意这里的“commercial”只是报纸名称中的刊物类别词，不是现代媒体佣金披露，也与唱机商业来源无关。 同报刊的1895年第250号再次提供期号与年份，链接和元数据层级可见；下一条改为1912年的Friulian民主报刊Il Paese，说明不是所有相似结果都同一刊物，也不能按局部片段混成同一馆藏条目。 Il Paese命中描述是1912年Friulian报刊，并将机器可读作者缺失另列；随后是一份1839年Javasche Courant殖民时期报纸。现有搜索列表明显按 Commons 文件名/内容对query作宽松匹配，数值3000与实体型号不可混同，需逐条查看元数据而非认为是命中唱机。 Javasche courant这一命中写明巴达维亚（Batavia）和荷属东印度/印度尼西亚发行范围，是具地域信息的历史期报；接着是1806年Leeuwarder courant。报刊检索结果的连续出现再次说明内容匹配非型号实体匹配。 Leeuwarder Courant之后的“Memoirs of the family of Grace”是较有解释力的误命中：对象为家族回忆录/插图目录，描述字段提到插图作者Dominique Vivant Denon，因此命中Denon并非Denon唱机；别名/字符串检索足以把人物名拉入结果。须继续完整读取该项与query全文，不能因看见Denon就误认实体匹配。 Grace家族回忆录的长描述明确列出插图者Dominique Vivant Denon，但作品主题仍是家族传记/版画插图；其PD元数据不能代表唱机素材。下一结果为荷兰画家词典，属于艺术家索引书，查询可通过人名Denon跨学科命中。 荷兰艺术家词典的目录主题印证Denon人物名检索会匹配历史艺术书目，版权字段仍是书籍扫描元数据。随后最后条目为法语圣经历史教学微缩本，明确1868年与加拿大档案馆原版藏本，进一步属于教育文本而非设备。全文末段仍需读完以确认返回分页/JSON闭合结构。 教学史微缩本由Canadiana.org贡献、渥太华大学数字化赞助，许可字段标PD。接下来的大型德文神话词典主题是神话，不相关于产品图片；metadata里的当代上传日期/扫描对象年代不可混为作品年代。 德文神话词典含超过1500页及雕版插图说明，其许可为Public Domain Mark；该记录是书籍/插图扫描，仍不是Denon设备影像。此Commons查询结果完整响应显示大量旧书、报纸与艺术目录，且因Denon人名/3000字符串出现误命中。首遍到124,904字符末尾闭合，逐字读取覆盖完整。

passes.focus: 事实证据、许可边界与操作限制
passes.notes: 第二遍聚焦事实证据、许可与操作限制。原始查询字符串明确是精确词组Denon AND 3000；首项题名为1698分数理论书，所谓“PD old”及许可字段仅针对该扫描。它是明显非唱机候选，不能因短语检索或公有领域标注认定图片可用。 第一条的credit链接是扫描副本出处，不提供目标音频设备信息；许可元数据是扫描页当前声明。第二条Acta mathematica标示古老数学期刊/数学主题、无机器可读作者及Toronto扫描，依然离题；这类页面即使含清楚许可标签也不该作为目标对象素材。 第二项底层扫描由多伦多数学科学与渥太华数字化项目供给；第三项Government Printing Office出版的行政备注有US政府PD类别，来源虽看似可信但仅属另一个题名。审读许可时保留对象级边界，不能由政府PD类别推及目标设备图像，也不能仅按站点用户/上传行为。 Amsterdam报纸由Delpher/Internet Archive供数，具体时间与地域写明，许可归类为PD-old但仍是1811期刊扫描；该登记能支撑其自身版权主张，不证明目标素材。下一条转为古代史微缩讲座材料，两者标题、作者和数字化来源各自单独呈现。 微缩本目录写明原卷号、旧书馆藏类别和哥伦比亚大学图书馆数字化参与，许可字段指向Public Domain Mark。这种许可记录是具体文本扫描的类别信息，不能扩展到搜索query或其他同页结果。随后出现Napoleon medal目录扫描，同为藏书类结果。 California Digital Library扫描书的题名实际描述拿破仑时期奖章目录，表明搜索里出现Napoleon这一语义相关词但不等于设备素材。许可标PD-US expired应用于此书。接着是意大利文乌菲齐绘画收藏目录，作者/收藏机构与扫描出版信息独立列出。 乌菲齐目录标绘画主题、分册出版年份范围和PD-US expired，但这些是目录出版元数据而非图像中每幅画的再利用确认。后续美国印第安人词典的标题与词典类别清晰、版权元数据PD，亦与设备无涉；要分别看出版对象/扫描文件和具体用途。 Smithsonian词典作者为美国民族学局、日期1903且PD字段只描述该历史词典。Béraldi藏品目录描述统计12,000幅肖像版画、800/1,000幅版画及“3000件”19世纪印刷品/杂项，提供query中3000的另一个语义来源；它还可能在长文字/图书关系内提及Denon，但该文件明确是版画/书籍目录，不能被当唱机照片命中。 3000文本命中已确认会来自某些馆藏描述中的收藏数量（如3000件19世纪ephemera），而另一条是1667年算术教材扫描，microfilm注记明确资料介质。该类数字检索并不构成Denon DP-3000NE的型号匹配；要保持“搜索原始命中”与可发布素材审核的区分。 Hofstede de Groot作品目录的PD-Art标注针对目录数字化品及其旧版绘画清单，不能泛化到任意画作图片。其后Il Friuli 1886期报纸属历史期刊，标题中的“commerciale”描述刊物栏目/类型，不是商业交易或单篇商业披露。 两个Il Friuli期号分别为1886与1895，虽然元数据列Public domain，仍需与电子产品具体图片/作者/拍摄来源匹配后才能判断许可。被查询的文件名和扫描类别均指向历史报刊，不能以其公共领域状态填充目标唱机资料。 Il Friuli 1895期号页面再次将扫描下载、出版日期和PD状态标给单一期刊。随后1912年Il Paese被标为民主运动机关报，说明即使连续同地区出版物仍是不同期刊对象、单独权属字段。 Il Paese日期记录与作者字段缺失被分开，PD条目不替代准确作者归属；下一报纸命中是1839年Javasche Courant，标题和期号显示印度尼西亚/巴达维亚地方出版史。它只是query的另一个历史刊物命中，并非设备图像或权利依据。 Javasche命中由Delpher/Internet Archive共同列出处，标出Batavia、Landsdrukkerij和1839期号；许可范围仍不通用。下一条是1806年Leeuwarder Courant，这些记录再次表明query对相同馆藏语料进行宽泛字符串匹配而非专门唱机文件检索。 Leeuwarder报纸的档案转存链接和PD-old类别仅说明这一期1806地区报纸。Grace家族回忆录再次因Dominique Vivant Denon插图作者名匹配“Denon”，但作品本体是多语家族回忆录/版画与音乐资料，许可PD US expired只针对其扫描条目；这将检索误命中机制具体化，仍不能说它是唱机图像。 回忆录条目确有Denon人名在所列众多画家/插图者中，credit仍只指向该书数字扫描；许可并不使插图重新变成产品图。随后荷兰画家词典同样可因艺术家检索词命中，作者Wurzbach及卷册信息明确，元数据PD-US expired依附于书籍文件。 荷兰艺术词典为研究工具型书目，PD-US expired针对数字扫描条目；圣经史法语微缩课本标出1868年、加拿大公共档案馆原版和PD-old类别。各条目都有明确来源、对象和使用条件但无一是目标唱机图片；已完整复读到该文件长JSON闭合前最后段，接下来读末尾校验段。 法语圣经史教材的许可/贡献来源写明Canadiana.org与渥太华大学数字化，不是作品创作者；最后的德文神话词典含1558页与130片插图，类别PD-old/Public Domain Mark针对扫描书。注意实际主体文本版权、原图权利与Commons元数据许可是不同层级；本查询响应仍未给出DP-3000NE具体图片可用结论。 最后条目Contributor为Wellcome Library并展示Public Domain Mark字段；此许可内容属于神话词典自身且不等于所有插图、版次或后续用途天然无条件可用。原始查询最终响应闭合完成，pass2覆盖全文。

passes.focus: 逐句文风候选及应保留的必要否定/历史原文理由
passes.notes: 第三遍逐句分析候选保留理由和历史信息。响应顶部只给出query“Denon AND 3000”及Commons分页继续标记；单靠查询词不构成真实设备/素材关联。首结果题名是1698算术书，元数据类别包括扫描未验证和旧版权类别，首屏就揭示搜索精度问题，须保留作为候选剔除依据。 分数教材条目的长题名、微缩介质和1698年旧书题名具体解释与唱机无关；虽然页面写Public domain，不能把这个词变成跨结果图像许可。下一项是数学期刊，仍无音频产品信息。 Acta mathematica的内容/贡献机构分别指向数学期刊和多伦多数学科学组，行政文档由GPO发布且政府PD类别。它们的短字段不足以关联唱机；保留题名、主题与来源属性是将误命中排除的必要依据。 1811报纸字段本身带有日期、出版地与媒体来源信息，作为历史档案条目清楚，但文学叙述不应将其和本批目标产品合并；即便公众领域字段很直观，也需要单条目级查验。下一条古代史讲座材料继续强化内容类型失配。 At 24500–28000 the remainder of the old-books result describes a microfilm lecture volume by Gustav Albert Sauppe, with Internet Archive/Columbia metadata and a PD designation tied to that scan. At 28000–31500, the query proceeds to a California Digital Library/IA description volume; the transition maintains the evidence that the returned set consists of unrelated digitized works, and all object-level license labels remain scoped to those files. The medal catalog attributed to Captain J. C. Laskey concerns Napoleon-era commemorative medals; despite an old-book scan carrying a PD-US label, its content and license metadata are not evidence for the turntable image. The next result is an Uffizi drawings catalog, another unrelated object whose own scan metadata should not be detached from the work. The Uffizi catalog entry gives serial fascicle dates from 1890 through 1897 and a PD-US scan label, clearly tied to this art catalog. A separate Dictionary of American Indians North of Mexico follows; its subject and standalone book-scan status reinforce that the text must retain the false-positive provenance rather than imply a product match. The Smithsonian Bureau of Ethnology dictionary is dated 1903 and credited as a digitized book; its PD status is likewise record-specific. The Béraldi 1872–1892 catalog entry explicitly mentions “3000” nineteenth-century ephemera, a plausible lexical cause for the query match, while being a book about prints and books rather than a Denon turntable. Forster’s arithmetick is explicitly a 1667 book scan, with sequential issue links and a microfilm-cover note; the 2026 Commons DateTime is an upload/metadata event, not publication date or evidence of product contemporaneity. Keep those distinctions visible rather than treating record timestamps as artifact dates. The next catalog raisonné concerns seventeenth-century Dutch painters; its PD-Art declaration is about reproductions of public-domain artworks and does not cover unrelated modern hardware imagery. The results then move to an 1886 Il Friuli newspaper, so date/title context remains a strong disambiguation cue. The Friuli entry includes its specific newspaper issue number 189 (1886), Italian periodical subjects and IA scan credit, followed by another 1895 issue. Its PD statement is attached to this historical newspaper scan; preserving the exact issue/year prevents conflating upload timestamps with publication dates. The second Friuli newspaper issue is explicitly number 250 from 1895; its awkward archive URL path is simply credited metadata, not an instruction or proof beyond that scanned record. The next file is Il Paese, an Italian Friulian-democracy newspaper issue dated 1912, clearly distinct in title and period. Il Paese’s 1912 issue 139 has no machine-readable author flag, and its public-domain marking belongs to that newspaper scan; preserving the qualification avoids overstating authorship or licensing. The result list then changes to Javasche courant dated 22 May 1839, another unmistakable historical periodical. Javasche courant specifies issue 41, Batavia, publisher Landsdrukkerij, and 22-05-1839, with separate IA and Delpher references; this is a fully described historical newspaper, not a device listing. Its neighboring Leeuwarder courant item is dated 20-08-1806 and explicitly gives Leeuwarden/local distribution, further emphasizing the query false positives. Leeuwarder’s entry gives archive and Delpher citations while retaining the object-specific 1806 title/date; these source references are provenance, not instructions to follow. The Memoirs of the family of Grace record is a book scan; its illustrator list includes Dominique Vivant Denon, which directly explains why “Denon” can appear in this query result without any relation to Denon-branded electronics. The Grace book’s long illustration and contents list explicitly names Dominique Vivant Denon among portrait artists, a genuine name collision behind the search result; this specific scan’s PD label cannot be generalized. Next is a German Dutch-artists lexicon issued in parts and describing three volumes, a bibliographic work unrelated to the product. The German lexicon’s dates and parts/volumes establish a multi-volume art reference book; its public-domain metadata only applies to this scan. The French religious-history microform begins at 112000 and identifies an 1868 original held in Canadian archives; that textual context and its PD-old category should remain explicit rather than being treated as potential device imagery. The French school religious-history scan credits Canadiana.org and the University of Ottawa and bears a public-domain status for this item. The final result is a German mythology dictionary by Wilhelm Vollmer, with extensive page/plate counts and Wellcome Library contribution; its PD mark belongs to this scanned historical book. These concluding records illustrate why preserving the full query-result context and not borrowing its license metadata matters.

[3500,7000)：ER-4到EC-36、Sharp R-10的选择依据由加热机制对照推进；重点是避免1956出口型号混淆、把商用微波炉误写作家庭普及。A700逐型生产区间明确，故事语气保持事实与策展解释分离。多项媒体未获许可、销量/群体经验/劳动时间不证实，保留这些具体否定。
[7000,10500)：A700条目结束后进入HL1和Hoover，保留MoMA与Pompidou不同条目版本（HL1与HL1/11）以及Hoover“约1956–59实物制造区间”，不是全球首发；广告存档只补证仍售而非首发。共同否定图权、销量、群体体验未核是必要文风。
[10500,14000)：Model 500用拨盘周边字码和底座/听筒分工解释对象；排除1500/2500键盘型号。Ericofon从1946开发到1954试产、1956生产再到MoMA年代范围分层，不将其直接说成全球首售；NAV1000明确用制造年而非常见首发说法，并排除NAV1200。避免把事实项变成宣传排序或进步直线。
[14000,17500)：NAV1000结尾的公共影响边界将GPS功能与道路/飞行安全、全球普及分离；GO初代更明确排除后续GO300和现款。寻呼候选限定通知再回拨而非双向会话，AirPort先由固定网络端与移动电脑关系提出策展意义，日期仍只公布/计划。
[17500,21000)：AirPort日本改名/计划供货不作实际销售；FRITZ!Box初代无WLAN，秋季版另计，解释宽带整合但不声明后代协议能力。Picturephone ModII限定匹兹堡商业服务及专用线路，不与1964展览机混淆。强调单机服务、安全或普及效果未经实测，文风不做线性演进或网络平台宣传。
[21000,24500)：Solar Mower文字引用原厂1995销售但明确不借后代效率数或宣传首次，未作现机/当代服务测试。AIBO把MemoryStick本地程序与云服务时代分开，公布日期/后续销售数量不推出普遍陪伴体验。GPS155批准是TSO事件、不是FAA原证书的独立复核，也不代表现在飞行安全或全部型号兼容。
[24500,28000)：SMART Brailler与1951 Classic区分电子反馈功能，但不写教学效果；Nest初代日期是博物馆作品年代，厂商公告只佐证2012仍售/代际结构。Hue套装的当地开售是安排，协议与软件状态不保证今天服务，亮度/场景不等节能或健康效果。所有媒体/证据状态仍是文字候选，非展品许可。
[28000,31500)：Hue证据使用identity/dateSource分列，且不保证地区/当前服务；Echo条目以邀请制到公开订购作为服务/商业历史而非销量趋势结论；Google Home明确只有公布预订和供货计划，后代服务版本不可并入初代。
[31500,35000)：Nest Protect把CPSC确认日期/召回更新与厂商功能公告分开；召回未报告伤害是记录边界而非风险不存在结论。HEM-1的“电子但手动”区分具有防误读作用，不转写成医疗精准度建议。Nabaztag初代无麦克风、保留v1日期来源差异，不移入后代语音；产品本体与网络服务寿命是不同时间轴。
[35000,38500)：DC01句式把产品结构/生产节点与“永不减吸力”宣传切开；DIRIGERA的荷兰现售与全球计划分层，Matter-ready不是同期完整实现；FP2的雷达分区输入强调非摄像，但与跌倒模式/多人区用途不能混用，避免医疗/安全承诺。
[38500,42000)：TM5用途是步骤引导而非首创或效果结论；POCKETALK W通信套餐/地区配置区别和WiFi更新限制必须保留，否则读者会误解设备离线可用；Stream3的2024目录只锚在售/代际、不声称首发，后续15小时也是厂商标称。整体文风以克制“无需声称”限制观点扩张。
At 42,000–49,000, Victor Reader nominal battery figure is catalog/manufacturer context rather than a measured result; preserve bounded provenance. Airfryer HD9220/40 is a German 230V product-existence/spec-sheet anchor, not a global launch or health-effect claim. S10 is an initial one-week domestic review; preserve its reported ~3-hour recharge, absent mop-only mode, plumbing/water-station caveats, and disclosed affiliate commission without inflating these into long-term reliability or sponsorship claims. FP400 release material supports a dated sale and bounded Matter/Thread functions, with Pro vs standard distinction; it is not a hands-on test. GE monitor-top and Bendix remain discovery leads because identity/model evidence is incomplete.
At 49,000–52,500, the Garmin GPS 100 remains a discovery candidate with disputed 1990/1991 chronology and a JS-only manufacturer page; the record correctly refuses to substitute a screenshot date for launch. AirPort Express (2004) is tied to a dated announcement and expected July availability, explicitly not confirmed delivery; keep its later 2008 802.11n materials separate. Google Wifi is anchored to an announcement/preorder plan, with no contemporaneous sale/test evidence and a missing independent source role; preserve as pending rather than formal.
At 52,500–56,000, Braille Bloom is retained as a 2026 accessibility lead from article navigation only; the record explicitly withholds claims of delivery, electronics, or model. Thermomix TM7 is likewise only an index-supported lead because the source PDF failed to load and key parameters were not read; inclusion is not inferred from TM5. Source inventory begins at the end of the range, carrying dated check metadata and explicit verification limits; preserve those limits alongside source identity.
At 56,000–59,500, source records distinguish museum object-level evidence from manufacturer histories and preserve retrieval limitations: Toastmaster exact-model claims are based on returned institutional index text because the page/PDF errored, while the 1A1 cross-reference is explicitly same-institution. The ER-4 record identifies the Japan Electrical Manufacturers’ Association as survey source, so institutional hosting is not misrepresented as independent experimental research. Toshiba/Panasonic history sources retain their brand-promotion character and bounded scope.
At 59,500–63,000, the R-10 museum record’s manufacturer-supplied survey origin is explicitly not an independent test; Kenwood support/history pages are separated as sales-support versus brand history for A700 dating. HL1 evidence uses distinct museum catalogs, while Pompidou is limited to its index after an Internal Error and does not generalize the /11 suffix to all electrical versions. Constellation dating is approximate and its 1965 newspaper ad is evidence of continued sale, not launch; the PDF retrieval limit and image copyright are retained.
At 63,000–66,500, sources distinguish 500 telephone museum/display evidence from unsupported durability and adoption rhetoric; the altered photo background is disclosed. Ericsson factory history and MoMA object catalog serve different corroborating roles for Ericofon, with the latter’s work dates bounded as 1949–1959. NAV1000 museum and archival records are limited to index text after Internal Errors; the archive directory does not mean the underlying engineering files were read. TomTom annual-report evidence begins with the original GO launch and carefully prevents aggregate product sales from being attributed to one model.
At 66,500–70,000, TomTom’s CEO Hall of Fame story is not evidence of a product award; preserve that distinction. The PageBoy historical timeline and exhibit corroborate model-era context, but the exhibit photo source (eBay) and image/background processing are explicitly not electrical-version proof. Apple’s Canada AirPort announcement and Japan naming/trademark notice have separate regional scopes; the latter’s 2000 plan must not be cast as a global first launch. FRITZ! sources separate an anniversary announcement from the maker’s product-evolution chronology, with manufacturer-promotional character retained.
At 70,000–73,500, Picturephone documentation is attributed to a CMU project group hosting AT&T archive material; same-project dependence and image rights remain visible, and the dubious 0.8MP figure is expressly excluded. Husqvarna’s 1995 Solar Mower claims are manufacturer history, with later production/energy metrics not assigned to the first model. Sony’s May announcement and October follow-up distinguish ERS-110 launch plan from reported June sales and ERS-111; Garmin GPS155 TSO approval is a maker retrospective without independent FAA certificate review, and current inventory is not promised.
At 73,500–77,000, Perkins sources are from the institution that makes/promotes the Brailler; the Classic product’s cumulative figures are not treated as SMART Brailler sales, and independent educational outcomes are absent. Nest evidence pairs a museum object record with the maker’s 2012 follow-up, which supports ongoing sale and model-generation distinction but not service durability or group impact. Philips hue’s announcement and factsheet document the initial kit/features; Japanese-language collateral does not establish Japan availability. Echo source is Amazon retrospective, not independent service-history evidence.
At 77,000–80,500, Amazon’s 2015 open-order announcement is distinct from invitation-only introduction; customer praise remains quoted company material rather than independent evaluation. Google Home announcement and Assistant ecosystem description establish planned features/supply and positioning, not independent performance or durable service. Nest Protect combines regulatory recall scope with maker launch design; CPSC’s 403 limits direct rereading and should remain explicit. Omron sources distinguish manual HEM1 (1973) from electronic generation and later 1978 models, avoiding conflation.
At 80,500–84,000, V&A’s Nabaztag object research is stronger for the physical 2005 artifact, but its service-shutdown date is not treated as an undisputed global endpoint. The community-hosted archive preserves original promotional copy while current maintainer identity remains uncertain. Dyson’s own production timeline and James Dyson recollection are both maker-linked sources, not independent durability evidence. IKEA Netherlands later-edited live-sales content is not retroactive proof of Matter support; global announcement distinguishes May announcement from October plan. Aqara FP2 release/manual evidence is bounded to product capabilities and explicitly non-medical.
At 84,000–87,500, the Aqara manual is maker operating guidance with region/hub/installation constraints, not a real-world compatibility test. Vorwerk’s annual report dates TM5 market introduction to September 2014; company-relayed praise is not independent review, and Cook-Key is kept out of the initial configuration. Sourcenext separates Japan actual-sale date and SKU/eSIM/network restrictions from later software-update requirements. Victor Reader evidence distinguishes exact Stream 3 from a 2024 catalog existence anchor, explicitly not launch timing; 2025 upload path is not converted into release date.
At 87,500–91,000, Philips’ Airfryer datasheet date is a model-existence anchor, not worldwide first sale or health evidence; the product archive is later/current manufacturer context. SwitchBot’s S10 retrospective separates IFA/crowdfunding from formal launch, while its live page may have changed; The Verge review supplies a dated one-week hands-on snapshot and affiliate disclosure, not longevity. Aqara FP400 availability and official-forum post constrain geography (excluding RU/JP) and third-party Thread semantics; keep FP400 distinct from FP400 Pro and company forum material non-independent. Monitor-Top remains a discovery entry awaiting exact model identity.
At 91,000–94,500, Maine’s roughly 1927 monitor-top refrigerator record lacks a precise model/plate and cannot fill a formal refrigerator gap by series-name inference. Laundry object #327 documents a pre-1937 front-loader but not Deluxe/Standard variant; retain need for contemporary model-specific manual. GPS 100’s exact 1990/1991 date remains unresolved because the maker history is only a JS shell. AirPort Express is an announcement with expected July delivery, not verified shipment, and later 802.11n manual material must not be mixed in. Google Wifi likewise has announced mesh/app and preorder plan only, with sale/test evidence absent. Braille Bloom navigation and TM7 index/PDF-error are strictly discovery signals, not verified delivery or detailed specs.
At 94,500–98,000, the ER-4 exhibit prose carefully limits the Japan-specific 1955 sale date and separates identity/date evidence from interpretation. Context and significance explicitly mark curatorial comparisons (EC-36, TM5) rather than linear inevitability or population-wide adoption. The design section explains the water/temperature control relationship while warning that diagrams would be interpretive and archival image rights remain uncleared. Usage text deliberately avoids an unverified operating recipe or repair instructions and flags unknown specimen electrical/insulation condition; limitations deny inferred sales, social effects, safety, and media clearance. Preserve this layered boundary-setting rather than shortening away the caveats.
At 98,000–101,500, the Ericofon draft keeps 1956 mass production distinct from 1954 trial manufacture, 1953 exhibition, and MoMA’s broad 1949–1959 object date; no global first-sale inference is made. The narrative explicitly places fixed-line use within operator infrastructure, and the design/usage sections avoid turning manufacturer comfort or impact claims into measurements, while qualifying region-dependent bell configurations and refusing modern-network hookup steps without manual/testing. Style candidates worth retaining include the concrete action sequence (“拿起、翻看底部拨盘、进行拨号以及重新放置”) and careful analogies bounded against direct inheritance; necessary negatives include no comfort universalization, no modern connection instruction, no sales/accessibility claims, and no media-clearance inference from a visible image.
At 101,500–102,808, paragraph-level provenance stays consistently assigned to the two named records for each section. The ending limitations preserve key editorial negatives: a selection suggestion is not a ready/published exhibit; same-maker sources are not independent corroboration; discovery candidates do not inflate formal counts; image viewing is not permission; and index/403 retrieval limits remain visible. The category coverage caveat explicitly acknowledges refrigerator/laundry evidence gaps instead of claiming balanced coverage.

passes.focus: 来源、日期、型号及其适用范围
passes.notes: Opening query is the broad “Hamilton Pulsar” Commons search, checked 2026-10-15, with 30-result continuation. First displayed match is a 2009 Nissan Pulsar GTI-R racing photo, explicitly described as an autoslalom scene and CC BY 2.0 with attribution required; the adjacent Bajaj Pulsar result is a motorcycle. These early lexical false positives matter for preserving why the data must not imply product identity. The motorcycle result has a user description (“this is bajaj pusar”), 2010 original date and CC BY-SA 3.0 own-work credit, all tied to that photograph. The next “pulsar” result is an X-ray image of the Crab Nebula: its description explains the neutron star and Chandra observatory, showing a further scientific meaning of the term unrelated to either the Hamilton watch or consumer devices. The Crab Nebula metadata includes a Smithsonian “No known copyright restrictions” usage statement while still marking the item copyrighted; that nuanced wording applies only to this NASA/Chandra image and should not be flattened into a blanket rights claim. The next hit is explicitly a Nissan Pulsar GTI-R engine bay, dated 2018 and CC BY-SA 4.0; it is automotive subject matter and a clearly distinct licensed photo. Premios Pulsar 2017 is an award-event name visible in metadata, with photographer Carlos Figueroa and CC BY-SA 4.0 terms; the entity is a Chilean music awards event, not the Hamilton Pulsar watch. A following Villa Cariño event photograph uses the same award title, demonstrating repeated event-keyword hits rather than the requested device. The Villa Cariño record repeats the award-event context and author/license metadata. A much more relevant lexical hit is PulsarLED: its description identifies a circa-1976 Pulsar Touch/Command ladies’ LED watch, but still does not identify the Hamilton Pulsar P1 or verify its model/version; the photo’s CC BY-SA 3.0 permission is image-specific and attribution is required. PulsarTimeComputer is a circa-mid-1970s men’s LED watch and is closer semantically, but its entry still does not establish the specific Hamilton P1 identity; its 2021 Commons metadata date is not the watch’s creation date. The next generic “Pulsar - 020” entry belongs to watch category but requires inspecting its actual description/model before treating it as relevant; title/category alone are insufficient. The Jamin gallery records titled Pulsar - 020 and Pulsar - 0200 are indeed watch photographs (French description “Montre Pulsar”), with CC BY-SA 3.0 attribution requirements. But generic brand identification does not prove Hamilton P1 model, so retain as potentially related but unverified, not as a verified P1 match; the sequence then continues to another numbered watch photo. The third numbered Jamin gallery item, Pulsar - 0201, remains described only as a Pulsar watch; do not infer model from sequence. The neighboring Pulsar_ result explicitly categorizes a Bajaj Pulsar motorcycle and repeats the uploader’s informal misspelling, another homonym that should not be normalized into the target watch. Pulsar 2 UF is explicitly in the watch category but simply described as “Pulsar”; the record lists photographer/CC BY-SA 3.0 rather than a model number. The next hit is a specifically named Dual Time World Chronograph, which should remain a different model from a P1 absent evidence tying them together. The Dual Time World Chronograph includes an explicit reuse permission requiring author/source/license credit close to the image, with CC BY-SA 3.0; that is a specific contemporary watch model and does not imply P1 identity. Another relevant-looking result is a Pulsar LED calculator watch held at World Museum Liverpool, described as made in the 1970s; it may be a related historical watch but remains a different identified artifact unless model confirmation exists. The second museum watch image repeats the circa-1970s calculator-watch description and credits a different photographer; both images carry CC BY 3.0 with attribution required. They are useful period/watch context but do not verify a particular Hamilton P1 variant. The next title “Pulsar Montre” appears to be another generic watch record, requiring attention to its own description and license. Pulsar Montre and Montre 1 are Jamin’s generic watch photos with CC BY-SA 3.0 and attribution; their lack of model identifiers means they cannot be represented as confirmed P1 evidence. The result sequence’s repeated gallery images also cautions against counting each near-duplicate as independent identification evidence. The Jamin series continues with Montre 2 (watch straps in categories) and Montre 3, still short generic descriptions rather than model identifiers. Because these are a grouped photo series, preserving their shared photographer/license and non-specific identification matters; do not overstate the number of independent product matches. Montre 3’s record closes with the same broad CC BY-SA 3.0 attribution terms; Montre 4 is another generic Pulsar watch photograph, now from a different camera and same uploader/gallery. The sequence’s repeated similar labels and same license are provenance clues but still lack a model-specific P1 designation. Montre 5 continues Jamin’s generic gallery and carries the same attribution share-alike terms. The next record explicitly names Pulsar P4 Time Computer 3215-2 and circa 1975; it is a model-specific historical watch entry but the P4 designation must not be confused with P1. The P4 image description states ref. 3215-2, stainless-steel men’s watch, circa 1975, made in the US; CC BY 4.0 requires attribution. Model number makes it specifically P4, not P1. Next is Pulsar_anim, but its entry describes a rotating neutron star animation, a scientific rather than horological meaning. Italian title identifies an 1980s Pulsar watch with 24-hour indicator, but not a P1; it is a recent photo under CC BY-SA 4.0. Next “Pulsar cronografo” signals a chronograph watch; wait for the entry’s full description/model/license before deciding relevance. Pulsar cronografo is described only as a chronograph and photographed in 2022; its share-alike terms apply to that photo. The German-labeled Pulsar uhr3 is another watch-category item but only described as “Pulsar,” with no model; it remains unverified for P1. The Joe Haupt vintage LED digital watch record identifies decade and collector provenance, with CC BY-SA 2.0 attribution/share-alike obligations, but no exact watch model. The next title names a Vintage Pulsar Model P2 Time Computer, showing a potentially informative model-specific adjacent artifact; P2 should not be conflated with P1. The Joe Haupt images explicitly identify Pulsar Model P2 Time Computer, one stainless steel with original band and both dated 2013 photos, each with CC BY-SA 2.0 obligations. They are the wrong model for P1; preserve the distinction rather than collapsing the brand-level match into the target.

passes.focus: 事实证据、许可边界与操作限制
passes.notes: Second pass re-examines the opening from evidence and permissions perspective: broad query/continuation gives non-target results; the 2009 Nissan rally photo has CC BY 2.0 with attribution required, while the Bajaj motorcycle match must be segregated. License belongs to each image record; no target-device rights follow from these search results. Rights check on the motorcycle photo: CC BY-SA 3.0 with attribution is specific to that uploader’s own-work image. The Crab Nebula search result is a Chandra X-ray image; its richly described astronomical content is not a watch, and its separate Smithsonian usage statement must not be conflated with the motorcycle license or any target asset permission. The Crab file’s date, Smithsonian source, and “no known copyright restrictions” wording coexist with Copyrighted=True; retain that nuanced caveat for this particular image. The following Nissan engine-bay photo is explicitly an automotive component and CC BY-SA 4.0, so neither title overlap nor its license supplies the sought watch asset. This part shows a Premios Pulsar 2017 event photograph of Stefan Kramer and CC BY-SA 4.0 attribution requirements. The following Villa Cariño entry is another event photograph under the same event series, not the Hamilton watch; even repeated “Pulsar” wording here is an award name. The second award-event photo repeats Carlos Figueroa’s CC BY-SA 4.0 record. PulsarLED, by contrast, is an explicitly identified circa-1976 ladies’ Touch/Command LED watch. Its image license is CC BY-SA 3.0, attribution required; it is a concrete historical Pulsar watch but still not labeled Hamilton P1, so preserve that necessary limitation. PulsarTimeComputer is explicitly a mid-1970s men’s LED watch, but no exact model number; its CC BY-SA 4.0 license needs attribution and share-alike, tied to Alison Cassidy’s photo. The next Jamin image is generically titled Pulsar - 020; its gallery context alone does not supply a specific model designation. The Jamin gallery records “Montre Pulsar” with CC BY-SA 3.0, attribution required. The next record continues with another numbered gallery image, also titled generically; neither identifies P1, and the shared artist/source means these should not be counted as independently verified model evidence. The Pulsar - 0201 record remains a generic watch image; its selected CC BY-SA 3.0 license requires attribution and share-alike. The next Pulsar_ record is categorized Bajaj Pulsar and text says “bajaj pusar,” which makes its motorbike interpretation explicit; the spelling as recorded should be retained rather than silently correcting historical metadata. “Pulsar 2 UF” is a watch-category entry, only described as “Pulsar,” with CC BY-SA 3.0. It offers no P1 identification. The next dual-time world chronograph is a separately named watch product, and rights verification for its photo must be assessed on its own record. The chronograph’s explicit photographer permission requires author, source and CC BY-SA 3.0 license credit close to the image; this must be retained if that photo is reused. The museum calculator-watch entry is another 1970s item, but its exact line-up/caption carries World Museum provenance and must be distinguished from the exact target watch. Second museum photograph is again a 1970s Pulsar LED calculator watch, with CC BY 3.0 attribution required; this permission is tied to the second museum image file. The following entries return to generic “Pulsar Montre” gallery items, so their model attribution remains undetermined. The generic Pulsar Montre image is CC BY-SA 3.0, requiring attribution and share-alike. Montre 1 repeats the same uploader, watch category and broad caption, so its model remains unknown; retain the uncertainty and avoid presenting gallery repetition as model validation. Montre 2’s specific extra “Watch straps” category does not establish a model; the same generic photo description and CC BY-SA terms continue. Montre 3 begins as another same-gallery watch image; preserve it as a separate catalog object but not as a separate confirmed target model. Montre 3 closes with generic description and attribution-required CC BY-SA 3.0. Montre 4 is another gallery photo; the camera metadata and time-in-frame differ, but the caption still does not identify a model. The record sequence should preserve such metadata without elevating them to stronger factual claims. Montre 5 repeats generic model identity and the Jamin CC BY-SA 3.0 terms. The P4 Time Computer entry is an explicit distinct model and is described circa 1975; the model-number difference from P1 is a critical boundary in using the search results as evidence. Rights for the P4 photograph are CC BY 4.0 with attribution required; its detailed text specifies model 3215-2, not P1. The next Pulsar_anim is a computer-generated astronomical video about a rotating neutron star, with CC BY-SA terms; its scientific meaning is another strict false positive. The 1980s watch with 24-hour indicator is only titled by decade/features, dated as a recent photograph, and CC BY-SA 4.0; not enough to establish P1. Next chronograph photo has location coordinates and a 2022 image date, but the metadata still does not name a historical product model. The chronograph entry is a recent photo by Clyde94 with CC BY-SA 4.0 and attribution requirements; the date/location are photo metadata rather than historical manufacture facts. The neighboring Pulsar uhr3 watch image is dated 2010 and is only generically labeled, under CC BY-SA 3.0, so it cannot verify P1. The Joe Haupt 1970s men’s LED watch is CC BY-SA 2.0 with attribution, but lacks model specificity. Both following objects explicitly say Pulsar Model P2 Time Computer and document separate views/photos; their CC BY-SA 2.0 terms apply to those Flickr images. The repeated P2 title is strong evidence that the dataset contains model-specific adjacent watches, and the text must preserve the P2/P1 distinction.

passes.focus: 逐句文风候选及应保留的必要否定/历史原文理由
passes.notes: Third pass focuses on wording and retention: preserve the broad exact query “Hamilton Pulsar,” checked-on date and result ordering/continuation as archived rather than editing the historic payload. The first item’s highly specific Nissan GTI-R caption and CC BY 2.0 metadata provide a concrete false-positive example; keep the attribution requirement attached to that photo. The Bajaj caption’s lowercase misspelling is part of the archived description and should not be silently rewritten during a historical review. The Crab text’s long astronomy prose and source date demonstrate a different semantic domain; retaining this exact kind of false-positive example explains why query results cannot stand alone as evidence. Preserve the Smithsonian image’s paired phrases “No restrictions” and “No known copyright restrictions” together with Copyrighted=True rather than normalizing away nuance. The next Nissan engine photo is explicitly an engine bay dated 2018; the technical specificity and make/model categories show the search is matching a car name, not the Hamilton watch. The Stefan Kramer image’s 2017 award title is a semantic false positive, and its license fields require attribution/share-alike; the next Villa Cariño image repeats the same event context. Preserve the event-vs-product distinction and individual photo license rather than summarizing both as watch images. The second 2017 ceremony photograph is quality-assessed, but that assessment applies to the event image rather than to product evidence. The Touch/Command ladies’ LED watch description is a valuable related historical fact; keep the actual 1976 approximate date and exact line-up, while not rewriting it into P1. The 1970s Time Computer is described in careful approximate-period language and with its own uploader/license; maintain that qualifier. The next title “Pulsar - 020” is a catalog filename and not a model assertion; the plain caption, not numbering, should govern the evidence statement. The generic French “Montre Pulsar” phrasing remains model-agnostic and the Jamin file is CC BY-SA 3.0.
